reasoning: Multiple evidence points strongly suggest IPO activity resumed on Chinese exchanges before January 2016, including CSRC announcements and actual company listings.

evidence.fact: China suspended all IPO activity on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges in early July 2015 amid a severe stock market crash.
The Shanghai Composite Index lost approximately 32% of its value between June 12 and July 8, 2015, in what became known as the Chinese stock market crash.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) announced in late August 2015 that 28 companies had been approved for IPO and would be allowed to proceed with public offerings.
In November 2015, the CSRC officially confirmed the restart of IPO processes, ending the four-month suspension that had been in place since July.
The first batch of 10 companies began trading on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges in late November 2015, marking the formal resumption of IPO activity.
Zhongjian Technology completed its IPO on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on December 4, 2015, raising approximately 500 million yuan.
